# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s, 2026-03-14

**Prepared by:** <email>
**Status at handoff:** ONGOING — still failing at end of available logs (03:59:28Z). Not confirmed resolved.

---

## TL;DR

Gateway config deploy **dep-4471** flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `true`, which stopped connection reuse. The 20-connection pool saturated in ~37 seconds and never recovered. Every business route has been returning 503 since **02:14:18Z**. **Roll back dep-4471.**

---

## Root cause

Deploy **dep-4471** (gateway, a.novak, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation") applied config generation 118→119 at `02:13:41.234Z`, changing three keys:

```
gateway.pool.perRequest:    false -> true     <-- this one
gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000  -> 2500
gateway.log.sampleRate:     1.0   -> 1.0      (no-op)
```

With `perRequest=true` the gateway opens a fresh upstream connection per request instead of reusing pooled ones. Connections are never returned to idle, so the pool drains and stays drained. Confirmed by `03:02:30.904Z WARN pool connection churn: 4180 opens in the last 5m, baseline is 40` — ~100x normal.

Every 503 is paired 1:1 with the same error, and it is the **only** error type in the file:

```
ERROR pool  req-NNNNN ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)
```

Pool state before vs. after:

| time | stats |
|---|---|
| 02:10:58 | `size=20 in_use=10 idle=10 waiting=0` |
| 02:15:58 | `size=20 in_use=20 idle=0 waiting=12` |
| 03:10:58 | `size=20 in_use=20 idle=0 waiting=232` |

**Why we're confident:** the deploy summary names the mechanism ("connection-per-request"), the config line names the same flag, the reload is explicitly attributed to the deploy pipeline, and the churn warning shows exactly that behavior. Name-level, config-level, and behavioral agreement — not just timing.

## Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| **Config applied** | 02:13:41.234Z |
| **First symptom** | 02:14:14.920Z — `acquire slow: waited 100ms` |
| **First 503** | 02:14:18.972Z — `req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms` |
| **On-call paged** | 03:21:05.282Z — `error_rate 5m avg is 71%` (**67 min after onset**) |
| **Last data point** | 03:59:27.974Z — still failing |
| **Duration** | ≥1h45m, ongoing |
| **Volume** | 530 x 503 out of 1,228 requests |

**Blast radius — all five business routes, 106 x 503 each:**
`/v1/cart` · `/v1/session` · `/v1/catalog/search` · `/v1/orders` · `/v1/checkout`

Includes full checkout and order paths — assume **revenue impact**.

Failures are spread evenly across all four upstreams (accounts 133, catalog 133, billing 132, orders 132), which rules out any single upstream and confirms it's the gateway's own pool.

**Every single 200 after 02:14 is `/health`** (106 of them, `pool_wait=2ms`). Health checks bypass the pool, so the node kept passing health checks while serving nothing but errors — it was never pulled from rotation, and dep-4471's own deploy gate passed clean 19 seconds before the first 503.

Degradation is progressive: 503 latency 659ms → 850ms; slow-acquire waits 100ms → 890ms.

## Action: roll back dep-4471

Revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` (config generation 119 → 118).

- Take the other two keys back with it unless you have reason not to — `upstreamMs 2000→2500` is untested in isolation and `sampleRate` was a no-op.
- Recovery signal: `pool stats` showing `idle > 0` and `waiting=0`, and the churn warning clearing back toward the 40/5m baseline.
- A gateway restart alone may clear the pool but will **not** hold — the config would reapply on next reload.

**Before/after rollback, check nodes 1 and 2.** This log is `node-3 of 3`. Config generation 119 came from the deploy pipeline, so it almost certainly landed fleet-wide, but I have no direct evidence for the other two nodes. If all three are affected, the customer-facing impact is 100% of business traffic, not one-third.

## Also needs attention

**1. Two deploys shipped into the active incident.** dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc, 03:20) both went out while the gateway was failing ~71% of traffic. dep-4473 landed 5 minutes *before* on-call was even paged, so nobody necessarily knew. Neither can be the cause — both postdate onset — but check whether either needs unwinding, and this is a deploy-freeze/health-gate gap worth a ticket.

**2. `/health` doesn't touch the pool.** This is the reason a fully-broken node stayed in rotation and the deploy gate went green. The readiness check should exercise a pooled dependency.

**3. 67-minute detection gap.** Alerting fired at 71% error rate; a 100%-of-business-traffic failure ran for over an hour first.

**4. Separate, unrelated worker slowdown — do not conflate with this incident.** Worker job duration degrades linearly at +110ms per 10 minutes, from 327ms to 2,197ms (**6.7x**), still climbing at end of log. It holds that exact slope from 01:00, **1h14m before the gateway broke**, and passes through 02:14 with no inflection — so it is not fallout. Workers are otherwise healthy: 1,080/1,080 jobs `finished ok`, contiguous job IDs (nothing dropped), flat 60 jobs/10min throughput throughout the outage, DB pool idle at `in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0`, `db_wait` flat at ~5ms. dep-4470 (worker, 00:48–00:55, "retry backoff for webhook jobs") is the obvious suspect but **unconfirmed** — the log starts after that deploy so there's no baseline, and the drift is uniform across all six job types rather than concentrated in `webhook`. Needs pre-00:48 worker logs. Own ticket, not a blocker for the gateway rollback.

## Caveats for whoever picks this up

- Single node's view (node-3 of 3); other nodes unverified.
- Logs end 03:59:28 with the failure ongoing — current state unknown, re-check before acting.
- `deploys.csv` has no rollback rows, so I can't tell whether dep-4471 was already reverted after 03:59.
- Minor logging artifact: the `pool stats` line at 03:15:58 reads `waiting=12` while per-request errors at that moment report `waiting≈196`. The counter resets/wraps; 503s continue unbroken. Not a partial recovery — don't read it as one.
